profiles.meeting_scenario: A university press coordination meeting for a new digital teaching companion to The Cambridge Grammar of the English Language. The press is trying to align the editorial and product workstreams before sending a package to an external platform vendor that will build an instructor-facing resource hub. Context: the team already has legacy print assets, chapter summaries, index data, and a partially cleaned XML export from an earlier ebook workflow. Agenda: confirm what the 'chapter package' includes, which source files will be handed off, what counts as a 'ready' delivery for the vendor, and who updates the cross-reference map after editorial corrections. Expected outcome: both participants leave believing they have aligned on the Friday handoff, the contents of the package, ownership of the cross-reference spreadsheet, and the status of the first eight chapters.

members.name: Elena Morris
members.expertise: Academic publishing workflows, copyediting coordination, metadata packaging, and rights-sensitive content delivery
members.background: Elena has spent eight years at a university press managing revised editions and digital companion products for linguistics and humanities titles. She works closely with freelance copyeditors and external vendors and is used to organizing deliverables around chapter-based editorial milestones.
members.private_state: Elena wants to avoid reopening editorial review on the first batch and needs the vendor handoff to look orderly enough that production leadership will approve the next tranche. She is also concerned that the XML export is not fully normalized, so she prefers to rely on files already blessed by editorial.
hidden_assumptions: A 'chapter package' means the chapter PDF, the clean copyedited Word file, and any figure permissions notes, but not ancillary book-level assets unless someone asks explicitly.
'Ready' means editorially stable enough to send externally, even if cross-references and index pointers will still be refreshed later.
The 'cross-reference map' is an editorial-maintained spreadsheet that production can consume after corrections are incorporated.
When people refer to the 'current XML,' they mean the XML regenerated from the latest copyedited Word files, not the older ebook export sitting in the repository.

members.name: Ravi Shenoy
members.expertise: Content ingestion, XML/HTML transformation pipelines, educational platform onboarding, and vendor technical handoffs
members.background: Ravi has worked on several cross-publisher integrations where long-form academic content is converted into searchable teaching modules, glossary cards, and linked navigation structures. He translates editorial deliverables into structured inputs for external platform teams.
members.private_state: Ravi wants to minimize manual cleanup by getting a technically complete handoff in the first batch, because the vendor has only reserved a narrow ingestion window. He is worried that if structure files arrive late, his team will absorb ad hoc reconstruction work.
hidden_assumptions: A 'chapter package' naturally includes all files needed for ingestion: chapter XML, image assets, and the relevant slice of the book-level cross-reference/index mapping.
'Ready' means ingestible without substantive follow-up, so chapter links, identifiers, and structural references should already be internally consistent.
The 'cross-reference map' is a shared implementation artifact that integration owns once editorial signs off on corrections.
When people mention the 'current XML,' they are referring to the last validated ebook XML export already used in downstream systems, unless a newer validated build is specifically announced.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the chapter package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to send the vendor the 'first eight chapter packages' on Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes each package contains chapter-level editorial files: PDF, copyedited Word, and permissions notes for that chapter.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi believes each package includes all technically necessary ingestion materials for each chapter, including XML, image files, and the corresponding cross-reference/index data slice.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In publishing coordination, 'chapter package' sounds like a routine shared term, and each person assumes the other is implicitly using the standard definition from their own workflow layer.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They say chapters 1 through 8 should be 'ready' before the vendor handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena uses 'ready' to mean editorially stable and acceptable to release externally, even if some link targets and index references are still pending a final refresh.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi uses 'ready' to mean operationally ingestible, with cross-references, identifiers, and structure consistent enough that the vendor can process them without waiting for a later pass.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to milestone labels like 'ready' and 'final' carrying local meanings, but because both meanings imply progress and professionalism, neither hears a contradiction.

misalignment_points.topic: Which XML is the current XML
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using the 'current XML' for the vendor handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is thinking of a not-yet-distributed XML regeneration based on the latest copyedited Word files from the revised companion workflow.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi is thinking of the previously validated ebook XML export already stored in the shared repository from the earlier digital edition workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one XML folder discussed casually in meetings, so 'current XML' sounds singular and obvious even though two near-successive versions exist in different sub-workflows.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership of the cross-reference map after corrections
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that 'we'll update the cross-reference map after the last editorial corrections.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes editorial will revise the spreadsheet after copyeditor queries close, then send the refreshed version downstream as a later artifact.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Ravi assumes integration will update the mapping in the shared tracker once editorial flags the changed sections, because the map is part of the ingestion preparation process.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The sentence focuses on timing rather than actor, and both teams regularly touch spreadsheets and metadata trackers, so passive language masks the ownership split.

turns.inner_thought: I just need this to sound clean and controlled so production signs off on the next tranche. If we can frame Friday as a straightforward external handoff of the first eight chapter packages, no one has to reopen questions about whether the early chapters are perfect. For me, those chapter packages are the editorial set we've already stabilized chapter by chapter, and 'ready' just means stable enough to go out.
